title: Install blocker heatmap + owner swimlanes (standup notes)
body:
Standup: Tuesday 2026-11-02 — ad-hoc cross-team triage + heatmap review

Attendees: Marisol Chen (owner), Amit Kapoor (network), Sophie Martinez (infra), Liam O'Connor (field eng), Priya Nair (SRE), + observers from Solutions Eng and Customer Success.

Purpose: create a lightweight heatmap of current install blockers across active on-prem/VPC projects, assign clear owners (swimlanes), and capture short-term mitigations vs. long-term fixes. Intended to be a pragmatic sync doc we update weekly.

---
Summary/high-level takeaways:
- Biggest cross-cutting risk this week: KMS/HSM integration failures in mixed-cloud VPC installs (two customers). Root cause appears to be key wrapping negotiation mismatch + intermittent MTU fragmentation on peered transit network for the HSM appliance.
- Second-tier pain: telemetry gaps for KV cache warmup metrics — we cannot tell whether slow first-token latencies are due to model cold-start vs. customer network microbursts.
- We have a short-term workaround for HSM (force TLS1.2 endpoint and a transport-level MTU clamp) that gets customers back to green; long-term fix needs kernel-level MTU tuning guidance + a small patch to the installer to detect and advertise MSS.

Heatmap (severity / status / owner)
- SEV-1: Customer "OrbisFin" (on-prem private deployment) — HSM handshake failures causing tokenization service crash on PRD. Status: mitigation applied (MTU clamp) but not root-fixed. Owner: Amit K. Action: ENG-4237 assigned to Amit, ETA patch for installer 2026-11-09.
- SEV-2: Customer "LatticeHealth" (VPC isolated) — inter-AZ peering path changes dropped packets for HSM session renewal every ~6h. Status: temporary scheduled cron that rotates connections to avoid renew-time window. Owner: Liam O. Action: field-eng runbook note + customer scheduled downtime to apply BGP stabilization.
- SEV-2: Multiple customers (pilot pool) — missing KV cache telemetry (first-token latency spikes). Status: investigating. Owner: Sophie M. Action: instrument short-lived synthetic prompts, correlate with instance CPU steal/runqueue. Linked to PD-112.
- SEV-3: Onprem node provisioning slowness (image pull timeouts behind corporate proxy). Status: mitigated with pre-seeded images where possible. Owner: Priya N. Action: add proxy-check step to preflight and docs.

Owner swimlanes (who does what this week)
- Amit Kapoor (network/HSM): finish installer MSS/MTU detection patch, land PR, and run 2 verifications with OrbisFin staging. Primary deliverables: PR for installer + short KB for field (how to verify MTU and set clamp). Slack lead: @amitk.
- Sophie Martinez (infra/telemetry): add one-shot synthetic prompt generator to the agent that runs during post-install checks and emits first-token latencies to Datadog. Deliverable: synthetic-check script + dashboard panel. Owner will coordinate with Observability team for tagging.
- Liam O'Connor (field): coordinate scheduled maintenance windows for LatticeHealth and validate BGP changes after peer config. Deliverable: maintenance window confirmation + post-change connectivity report.
- Priya Nair (SRE): add proxy preflight check and improve installer logging for image pull retries (expose retry counts to logs and to the console). Deliverable: installer logline spec + PR.
- Marisol Chen (owner): maintain this doc, escalate any SEV-1 regressions to eng leadership, own customer comms for OrbisFin.

Open action items (quick list)
- [Amit] ENG-4237: installer MSS detection prototype (due 2026-11-05).
- [Sophie] PD-112: telemetry check script + dashboard (due 2026-11-07).
- [Liam] Confirm LatticeHealth window and test routing (due 2026-11-04).
- [Priya] Add proxy-check to preflight and include in runbook (due 2026-11-06).
- [Marisol] Compose customer-facing incident summary for OrbisFin with timelines and expected fix date (draft due 2026-11-03).

Notes / discoveries during triage
- HSM appliances sometimes expose differing MSS when behind NAT/edge-firewall devices. Observed difference between 1500 vs. 1420 path MTU on customer transit. We saw TLS fragmentation on RSA key-exchange messages triggering handshake resets.
- Quick win: forcing the HSM client to use smaller segments (via installer-env var) reduces handshake failures by ~95% in our lab repro.
- Installer currently logs at INFO for TLS failures; adding DEBUG with raw socket ERRNO will speed diagnosis for future cases.

Runbook excerpts (temporary guidance to field)
1) If HSM handshakes fail during provisioning: check path MTU between node and HSM appliance (tracepath/traceroute with -M if available).
2) Apply MTU clamp on Linux host: ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1420 (only after validating with network team).
3) Set env REDWOOD_HSM_MSS=1360 in installer for immediate mitigation (workaround-only, not for long term).
4) If behind corporate proxy causing pulls to fail: pre-seed images in /var/lib/rdw/images and set installer flag --skip-pull (field use only).

Telemetry gaps and proposed quick instrumentation
- Problem: first-token latency (FTL) often spikes after restart; we lack a trace that ties FTL to either model cold-start, JVM/engine JIT waits, or network stalls.
- Proposal: add synthetic-check during post-install that does: 1) send tiny prompt, 2) record kernel-level socket metrics, 3) record engine cold-start counters, 4) emit single Datadog event with tags (customer, node-id, test-id). Implementation estimate: 2 engineer-days.

Risks and decisions needed
- Do we accept a field-facing KB that recommends MTU clamping as a supported mitigation? That has risk (customer network side effects) but reduces SEV-1 uptime impact. Decision owner: Product + Security to sign off by 2026-11-06.
- Long-term: installer should attempt MSS discovery as part of preflight; this will require careful carrier/edge-case testing. Consider this part of the Q1 infra backlog if approved.

Customer comms (draft bullet points for OrbisFin)
- We have observed intermittent HSM handshake failures traced to path MTU differences between the HSM appliance and application hosts.
- Temporary mitigation applied (MTU clamp) which restores reliability; our engineers are building an installer update to detect and handle MSS in the long term.
- Expected timeline: installer patch for detection 2026-11-09, schedule for rollout after customer approval.

Misc notes / notes-to-self
- Follow up with Security on HSM mitigation wording (avoid encouraging customers to perform network changes without network team).
- Track any additional customers that show similar TLS resets; add to heatmap.
- Add a small checklist item in the install runbook: "Verify HSM session for 24h" post-install.

Next meeting: Friday 2026-11-06, 09:30 PT — quick sync to confirm ENG-4237 status and OrbisFin comms.
